title: Smart admission tiers with request hinting and soft-fail degradation
creator: Marco Jensen
description: Design and implement a multi-stage admission control system that uses request hints (priority, degraded-acceptable flag, and cost-sensitivity) to route traffic through adaptive queues and decide fast-path vs. soft-fail degradation. The goal is to reduce SLO burn during transient overloads and region failovers while preserving high-value requests. This ticket covers design decisions, implementation plan for the runtime admission layer, integration with routing policies for multi-region failover, and the rollout/feature flag strategy.
comments: 2026-01-12 — Kickoff: Aligning on goals with SRE and Serve Runtime. Agreed KPIs: 99th P99 token latency adherence, request success rate >= 99.5 for P0/P1, controlled SLO spend. Confluence design doc created: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Smart+Admission+Tiers

2026-01-20 — Spike results: microbench of queue latencies and admission decision cost. Admission logic adds ~200us median overhead; acceptable when applied before heavy KV/cache ops. Linked PR with benchmarking harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/3142

2026-01-28 — Design review with PM & Product: agreed on three admission tiers: realtime (P0), best-effort (P1), degraded-soft-fail (P2). Realtime gets strict SLO isolation and preemptive KV cache reservation. Best-effort uses adaptive batching and can accept higher tail latency. Degraded-soft-fail returns structured fallback payloads (cached summary or partial text) with explicit reason codes for callers.

2026-02-05 — Implementation note: added RequestHint header semantics to SDKs for optional priority and degrade_ok flags. Backwards compatible defaults: if header missing, treat as best-effort. Draft SDK change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/523

2026-02-14 — SRE requested circuit-breaker integration. We will wire admission decisions to existing circuit-breaker state machine so admission can be more aggressive when downstream model instances are unhealthy. Dependency ENG-14567 noted.

2026-02-21 — Canary plan: Start with internal traffic only. Metrics to watch: admitted_rate_by_tier, shed_rate_by_tier, p99_latency_by_tier, user-visible_error_rate, and SLO burn. Dashboards prepared: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd1234/admission-tiers

2026-02-28 — Blocker discovered in regional failover path: when routing switches region, KV cache reservations are unavailable for a short window causing spikes. Plan: fallback to degraded-soft-fail for realtime tier during region transition window. Follow-up task created ENG-15809 to add transient-region-transition mode.
